title: KV Cache for Efficient Autoregressive Attention

blocks.text: A KV cache appends only new projected keys and values along the sequence axis. The task is: Append projected K/V arrays of shape (B,H,T,D) to an optional (K,V) cache along the sequence axis. Return a new cache without modifying the inputs.

The inputs are `cache`, `new_keys`, `new_values`. Keep their roles separate while you trace the solution. The animation follows the supplied implementation, so every highlighted operation connects to code you can inspect.

blocks.text: Read each symbol as a value with a specific axis, time, rank, token, or state role. The code must preserve those roles. A compact formula does not remove the validation, masking, boundary, or state rules in the prompt.

Before following the implementation, identify the output's shape and meaning. Then identify which input values can affect one selected output. This gives you a testable mental model before the code adds implementation detail.
What changes in the boundary case
Return a new cache without modifying the inputs. Use the Trace control to switch between the normal path and this boundary focus. The algorithm does not get permission to invent an unstated fallback.

A useful test changes one condition while holding the remaining inputs fixed. Compare the output shape, state transition, valid edges, selected tokens, or returned status. This isolates the reason for the change.
